transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I… I’m here because after some nights of eating, I end up sitting there with crumbs and empty containers around me, and I feel so ashamed. Disgusted with myself, really. The next morning I can hardly pray, or look people at church in the eye.
Does this happen to you often, or was it just a few isolated nights?
It’s… not just a few nights. Since my friend passed, it’s been happening once or twice most weeks, I guess. I don’t think there’s been a month where it really stopped.
Do you feel like you're in control of your eating during these nights?
No… not really. Once I take that first bite, after the house is quiet, it’s like my good sense just… steps aside. I’ll be thinking, Belinda, stop now, and my hands still keep reaching for more.
Do you feel guilty or criticize yourself after these episodes of eating?

Yes… I do. Afterward I just sit there, seeing all the crumbs and empty containers, and I feel… ashamed. Disgusted with myself. Sometimes the next morning I can hardly pray, or look folks at church in the eye.
During these nights, do you feel like you're eating a lot more food than most people would in a similar period of time?

Yes… I think so. On a bad night, I might start with a plate of leftover casserole, and then… it just keeps going. Brownies, biscuits, chicken salad from the fridge. More than somebody would normally eat, I know that.
During these nights, do you feel like you're eating really fast?
Yes… I do. I eat fast, usually standing there at the kitchen counter. Sometimes I hardly even taste the pound cake or crackers, and I’ll realize I’m swallowing before I’ve really chewed right.
Do you ever try to get rid of the extra calories after one of these eating episodes, like by vomiting or exercising?
I… I’m not really sure how to answer that. I don’t think I’ve noticed doing anything like that, not in any planned way.
Do you usually eat these large amounts of food alone?

Yes… usually. If I’m at bridge or a church supper, I’ll just take a small plate in front of people. Then later, after everyone’s gone, I’ll go back to the kitchen and eat more of the leftovers where nobody can see me.
Do you ever try to make up for the extra calories after one of these episodes by using laxatives or diuretics?
I don’t think so… I mean, I don’t use things like that to make up for it. At least, not that I’m aware of.
Have these eating episodes affected your daily life or relationships in any significant way?

A little, yes. I’ve… started skipping some bridge nights, and I’ve said no to helping in the church kitchen sometimes. I get too worried someone will notice food’s gone, or… ask why I’m acting ashamed.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight over time due to these eating episodes?
I… I’m not really sure. I don’t weigh myself much anymore. My clothes feel different sometimes, but I couldn’t say exactly.
Have these episodes of eating been happening for more than 3 months?
Yes… I think so. It’s been about five months now, since my bridge partner—my friend from church—passed away.
On average, how many times a week do you have one of these episodes where you eat a large amount of food and feel like you're not in control?
Most weeks… maybe once or twice. Since my friend passed, it hasn’t really gone away for a whole month or anything. It just keeps coming back, usually late at night.
Do you ever try to make up for the extra calories after one of these episodes by fasting or strictly restricting what you eat the next day?
I don’t really know… I haven’t paid close attention to that. Sometimes I just don’t feel like eating much after, but I wouldn’t say I have a plan or anything.
Do you ever try to make up for the extra calories after one of these episodes by skipping meals the next day?
I’m not really sure. I might skip breakfast sometimes, but I don’t think I’m doing it on purpose to make up for anything.
Do you ever try to make up for the extra calories after one of these episodes by being extra physically active the next day?
I don’t think so… I mean, I don’t usually do extra exercise or anything the next day. I haven’t really noticed that.
Do you ever try to make up for the extra calories after one of these episodes by being less active or resting more the next day?
I… I’m not sure. I don’t think I rest more on purpose because of it. Maybe I’m tired sometimes, but I haven’t really connected it like that.
Do you ever try to make up for the extra calories after one of these episodes by following a very strict diet the next day?
I don’t think so. I mean, I might tell myself I should eat better, but I don’t really follow some strict diet the next day.
Do you ever try to make up for the extra calories after one of these episodes in any way?
I don’t really think so. I might feel bad about it, but I don’t have some specific thing I do to make up for it.
Do you think your eating episodes are ever followed by any behaviors intended to prevent weight gain?
I don’t think so… not that I’ve noticed. I mostly just feel bad afterward, but I don’t really do anything specific to stop weight gain.
